title: Pin change + telemetry negotiation toolkit
content:
Goal: practical playbook for negotiating tenant region-pin changes that balances contractual commitments, minimal customer disruption, and telemetry requirements for auditability.

Audience: Solutions Eng, Legal, SRE/Operator, Customer Success. Use during pre-sale contract redlines, onboarding, and live pin change ops.

Background / quick context (notes to self):
- Customers frequently ask to change a tenant region pin mid-contract (e.g., move tenant from eu-central -> europe-anchored US region for cost reasons, or vice versa for compliance).
- Pin change can be operationally expensive (data movement, re-anchoring caches, KMS key rewraps, SLA variance).
- We need clear telemetry to prove residency commitments during and after change for audits.
- This doc sits between legal clause templates and operator runbook: negotiation + observable acceptance criteria.

Core principles:
1) Minimal customer-visible downtime — aim for < 30m impact window for read-only paths; interactive sessions require session-stitch plan.
2) Observable evidence — every pin change must emit a standard audit bundle (events, snapshots, checksums).
3) Clear rollback criteria and a one-click rollback plan where possible.
4) Contract alignment — pricing/credits for migration effort must be explicit.

Negotiation checklist (pre-sign / amendment phase):
- Confirm desired final residency region(s) and whether it is a hard pin (hard legal requirement) or soft preference.
- Ask for anticipated daily token throughput and peak concurrent sessions for migration sizing.
- Decide who manages data egress costs: customer or Redwood? Put in clause if contestable.
- SLAs: define acceptable latency bounds during migration windows and whether temporary SLA relaxation is acceptable with credits.
- Audit evidence package: confirm customer acceptance criteria for proof of residency (see "Audit bundle" below).
- Schedule: set a target migration week (low traffic) and identify 2 fallback dates.
- Escrow/retention policy for snapshots if legal holds are required.

Suggested contract clause (copy-paste friendly) — negotiation starting point: 
"Redwood will perform Tenant Region Migration to the target region specified in Schedule A. Redwood will provide an Audit Bundle within 24 hours of migration completion containing (1) region-assignment event logs, (2) final KV-store checksums, (3) service endpoint resolution map, and (4) telemetry showing request routing prior to and after migration. Customer agrees to pay migration fees as set forth in Appendix B unless migration is required by Redwood-initiated deprecation. Migration windows will be mutually agreed and Redwood will provide a rollback procedure in the event of material service degradation."

Pricing / crediting model options to propose:
- Flat migration fee (covers operator hours and snapshot storage).
- Usage-credit model: waive next invoice token fees for X% of migrated traffic during the first week.
- Shared-cost: customer pays egress; Redwood subsidizes operator time for customers with active Enterprise plan.

Operational acceptance criteria (what engineering & SRE will verify):
- Region pin state machine reports final state = "pinned" to target region for all tenant shards.
- KV-store checksum delta within acceptable threshold (0 for strict; <0.01% for eventual) across primary/replica.
- No unpinned requests were routed to a non-approved jurisdiction during the documented migration window.
- End-to-end latency for 95th percentile across demo suite within agreed SLA.
- Audit bundle delivered and validated by customer within 48 hours.

Audit bundle (standardized content):
- timeline.csv: ordered timestamped events (begin_migration, pre_snapshot, snapshot_hash, cutover, post_validation, audit_bundle_delivered).
- routing_log_{window}.ndjson: all routed request metadata (request_id, src_country, resolved_region, model_shard, node_id). Fields must be pseudonymized for PII if present.
- checksum_manifest.json: KV checksums and sample keys for verification.
- topology_snapshot.txt: service component map and active endpoints (IPs redacted as needed).
- operator_notes.md: short free text with anomalies and mitigations.

Telemetry sampling plan (why this matters):
- Full dump of every request is unrealistic. We implement targeted sampling to provide strong statistical evidence while controlling cost.
- Default sampling strategy for migration events: 100% sampling for control-plane events and 10% sampling for data-plane requests during a 2h window around cutover. Adjust per customer risk profile.

Telemetry signals and retention (recommended):
- region_assertion_event (high priority) — immutable event when tenant pin flips; store for 2y for audit cases.
- request_routemap (sampled) — map of request->resolved_region; retention 90d (or per customer legal requirement).
- kv_checksum_manifest — stored with migration snapshot, retained per contractual archival policy.

Operator playbook (concise run steps) — runbook owner: SRE operator on-call + migration engineer:
1) Preflight (72–24h before): run staging cutover simulation using tenant shadow traffic. Confirm runbook and consent from CS.
2) Pre-snapshot (T-30m): disable nonessential writes, take KV snapshots, compute checksums, store snapshot in region-escrow bucket.
3) Cutover (T0): flip routing policy; emit region_assertion_event; start high-priority sampling window.
4) Post-cutover validation (T+5–T+120m): run routing_log checks, run end-to-end latency probes, compare checksums.
5) Deliver audit bundle (T+24h).
6) Monitor (T+24h to T+30d): increased telemetry alerts for any unpinned routing.
7) Rollback (criteria-based): if checksum mismatch > threshold OR >5% of requests routed to banned jurisdiction OR latency SLO breaches for >30m, trigger rollback.

Quick operator checklist (sticky):
- [ ] Confirm legal sign-off on migration window and credits
- [ ] Confirm KMS key policy and rewrap plan
- [ ] Pre-provision target region capacity
- [ ] Schedule Slack incident channel + stakeholder invite
- [ ] Prepare audit bundle template for this tenant

Simulation & tabletop scripts (for internal rehearsals):
- Sim 1: High-churn tenant, 10% sampled routing; verify rollback path under heavy load.
- Sim 2: Jurisdictional error injection: simulate a node accidentally advertising a wrong region; confirm detection and rollback timeline.
- Sim 3: KMS failover during replica rewrap; test snapshot recovery and rewrap fallback.

Open questions / decisions to make (for product/legal discussion):
- Do we standardize a migration price for SMBs vs Enterprise, or keep all negotiations ad hoc? (ops prefers simple tiered pricing).
- What is the maximum lawful-access proof we are willing to provide to customers vs what goes to legal on a case-by-case basis?
- Do we expose a self-service partial pin API for soft pins, or is this always ops-managed?

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- Add sample jq/ndjson queries for verifying routing_log (copy from observability team).
- Draft a small template for the audit bundle README explaining how to validate checksum_manifest (include example Python snippet).
- Sync with legal next Wed (2024-03-13) to lock suggested clause wording and migration credit policy.

Appendix: example validation snippet (conceptual)
- python pseudo: compare manifest hashes, sample 100 keys, and assert equality or list mismatches.
